name: Phygellus
title: One who turned away from Paul
summary: Phygellus was a Christian from the province of Asia who turned away from the apostle Paul at a time when Paul was imprisoned. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 2 Timothy 1:15, where Paul expresses sorrow that everyone in Asia, including Phygellus and Hermogenes, had deserted him. He represents those who abandoned the apostle in his hour of greatest need.

keyEvents.title: Phygellus turns away from Paul
keyEvents.description: Paul writes to Timothy that everyone in Asia has turned away from him, specifically mentioning Phygellus and Hermogenes as examples of this betrayal.

keyEvents.title: Contrast with Onesiphorus' loyalty
keyEvents.description: In contrast to Phygellus' betrayal, Paul highlights Onesiphorus as an example of faithful friendship. Onesiphorus sought out Paul in prison and was not ashamed of his chains.

keyEvents.title: Paul's exhortation to hold fast to the faith
keyEvents.description: In the same letter, Paul urges Timothy to hold fast to sound teaching and not to fall away as others had done, indirectly referring to people like Phygellus.

keyEvents.title: The context of Paul's imprisonment and suffering
keyEvents.description: Phygelus' apostasy occurred at a time when Paul was suffering in prison for the sake of the gospel. Paul urged Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony about the Lord or of Paul as a prisoner.
